claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is obtained by removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is initially an as-cast solid solution.
Removing Co shifts dislocation-pinning dynamics.
The Co-free alloy transitions to enhanced dislocation mobility at lower temperature or strain-rate conditions than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
In situ neutron diffraction can measure lattice-strain evolution associated with deformation.
A hyperbolic constitutive model can represent mechanical response across temperatures and strain rates.
Tensile testing should span room temperature to approximately 900 degrees Celsius and strain rates of about 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1.
Changes in temperature and loading rate produce dynamic lattice distortions and dislocation arrangements.
Dynamic lattice distortions and dislocation arrangements alter local strain fields as dislocation mobility changes.
At lower temperatures and strain rates, solute-induced lattice distortions pin dislocations more effectively.
The absence of Co reduces solute-induced dislocation pinning in FeNiCrMn.
Reduced pinning causes an earlier onset of dynamic dislocation mobility as temperature or strain rate increases.
The mobility transition will appear as a shift in lattice-strain evolution curves and hyperbolic-model parameters.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit earlier and more pronounced changes in lattice strain and dislocation-density indicators with increasing temperature and strain rate.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit a lower effective yield threshold and altered hyperbolic-model fits.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is an appropriate compositionally defined baseline for the comparison.
The proposed mechanism is applicable from room temperature to about 900 degrees Celsius and from about 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1 under non-oxidizing conditions.
Neutron-diffraction peak broadening can provide dislocation-density indicators in this comparison.
The controlled comparison requires both alloys to undergo identical temperature, strain-rate, atmosphere, and diffraction conditions.
Failure to observe a statistically significant earlier or different mobility transition in the Co-free alloy relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
